title: Doc Cheatham, Ernest Elliott and Tommy Morris's records
summary: He compares Cheatham to Swayzee and Mouse Randolph, and says Tommy Morris's records impressed him in Boston though he never met Morris.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I know Cheatham from way back. He come here with a clarinet player, and I don't remember his name... But him and Swayzee was buddies, you know. I think at that time Doc was playing saxophone, too. He used to play saxophone and trumpet. But he stuck with the trumpet. And the other fellow played the saxophone and clarinet. And he was a good clarinetist, he was a good musician, this other fellow. But his head went bad.
Do you remember an early clarinet player by the name of Ernest Elliott?
He was the early Twenties, I think.
Who did he play with? Anybody then?
Well, he played with Thomas Morris. He played with

Oh, that's before my time. Ernest Elliott. I don't know him. I never did meet him. But when you say Tommy Morris... That's before I come to New York. I was up in Boston and I ran across some of Tommy Morris' records, some of the records he had. When I was listening at 'em, I was very impressed with the records, and I always wanted to meet Tommy Morris. His records, they really impressed me; you know, them old records.
Sidney Bechet was on some of them.

Yeah, I don't know who was on 'em, but he put out some nice records -- to me, at that time. And I always wanted to meet Tommy Morris. I never did meet him. When I come to New York, I didn't hear nobody say nothin' about Tommy Morris -- you know, around musicians and things. And I was hanging around musicians and the clubs...

Well, I knew Happy. I met him when I first come here. Him and Gene Mikell and all of them, all of that group -- I met all of them. Tommy Morris, I never met him! I never met him. I heard I think two people in (?) mention his name, Tommy Morris. I don't even know who the two people were now. But he used to put out some nice records.
